name: Scalar Endpoint Adjective in a Resultative
pattern: resultative VP with an adjectival result construed as a reachable state

entry.name: Scalar Endpoint Adjective in a Resultative
entry.pattern: resultative VP with an adjectival result construed as a reachable state

1.definition: Presents the result as an attained point or region on a scale.

grounds.locator: discussion of result predicates and endpoint construal

projection.target: On the completed-event reading, the rail reaches contextual smoothness. Replacing smooth with a property that does not readily supply an attainable endpoint can lower acceptability even when the verb and object are unchanged.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: Doing something until it reaches a state
curious.summary: A describing word after the object can show the point on a scale that the action brought something to.
curious.body: In They polished the railing smooth, the word smooth tells you where the polishing ended up. The railing ended up smooth, and the sentence reports that it got there. The describing word works like a point on a scale, such as how smooth something is. According to this dictionary, swapping smooth for a quality that doesn't readily supply an endpoint can make the sentence less acceptable, even when the verb and object stay the same. The analysis is marked provisional.
curious.try: Think of something you can do to an object until it's clean, flat, dry or smooth. Say it as one sentence with the describing word last.

teacher.summary: Helps explain resultatives whose adjective names an attainable endpoint on a scale.
teacher.explain: In a resultative VP like polished the railing smooth, the adjective gives the result as an attained point or region on a scale. On the completed-event reading, the rail reaches contextual smoothness. This dictionary treats the pattern as a specialization of the object resultative, and notes that replacing smooth with a property that doesn't readily supply an attainable endpoint can lower acceptability, even with the same verb and object. Present the adjective as the state the action brings about.
teacher.terms: Traditional grammar sometimes speaks of a resultative predicate or result phrase. In this dictionary: scalar endpoint adjective in a resultative.

contrasts.note: No result is stated; compare with polished the railing smooth.

watch_for: A learner might read smooth in polished the railing smooth as describing how the polishing was done, when it names the state reached.
teacher.activity: Give students verb and object pairs (wipe the table, paint the fence, press the shirt). They add an adjective that names the state reached, then compare which adjectives name a clear endpoint.

child.hook: What do you call a table after you wipe it until it's clean?
child.explain: Some sentences end with a word that tells how things turned out. They polished the railing smooth. After the polishing, the railing was smooth.
child.play: Pick something to do, like wipe, wash or paint. Say what you did and add a word for how it ended up.

checked.note: Fixed: curious body no longer says the railing started out rough or dull (the entry does not specify an initial state).

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Scalar Endpoint Adjective in a Resultative." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/resultative-scalar-state-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, ef810bb).
